**Owner requirements.** The player builds a garage first. Its door replaces a fence section, opening a wide route between the camp and the field. After the garage is usable, a separate plot inside camp offers the snow truck for a substantial amount of obtainable World 1 resources. The player drives it. Its low horizontal blades damage eligible enemies, cut trees, and break stone and other mineable rock nodes. The truck has its own HP and can hold an unlimited amount of every resource type. Parking it inside the garage automatically transfers cargo to the storage house. If the truck is destroyed outside the camp, all cargo still held by the truck is lost. If the truck is destroyed inside camp, the remaining cargo stays recoverable from the wreck and can be hauled to the warehouse.
- The closed garage door blocks enemies and follows camp-gate repair rules. The truck blades switch off inside camp.

The truck offer remains unavailable until the correct garage generation is paid, complete, physically usable and linked to an existing storage house. Its separate in-camp plot uses a substantial bill selected from registered relevant materials. Existing `metal` means metal ore in the observed game; it must not be silently renamed to steel. `steel` may be used only after the catalogue contains a usable, obtainable steel producer and all its inputs. The words engine, wheel, blade and panel describe model parts; this package creates no inventory item called “parts,” “engine,” “tires” or similar.

Two distinct usable bidirectional pedestrian openings remain available. The garage cannot silently count as a replacement for both or block them when its door is closed, a truck is parked or a queue forms. Workers, pets, customer approaches and driver exit points need real unobstructed paths. The garage connects to the inner camp circulation through its authored access; door and wall placement must match every selected view.
# Snow truck and fence-line garage — practical feature specification

The garage is a substantial camp project. Its field-facing door occupies a chosen fence segment. The garage and parking bay sit inside the camp; the truck can leave and return through that broad opening while people retain their ordinary camp routes. Once the paid garage is complete and usable, a distinct purchase plot inside camp offers the truck with an exact, stable resource bill.

facts.finding: Newest observed gameplay is Build14 and already contains a driveable truck, input routing, physical movement/contact code, docking, outside loss, inside salvage and fixed garage-time quote selection. These paths were inspected, not executed in this source audit.
Live raw IDs remain wood, stone, meat, coal, slate, metal; metal display is Metal ore. No live iron_bars, sheet_metal, crude_oil or fuel balance exists in the fixed10-item truck cargo catalogue.
One existing raw ledger count is a ten-unit physical bundle. One saw/quarry cycle consumes one bundle and produces one product count. Decimal migration must preserve that denomination.
Coal is a mined raw resource. Fuel was a distinct authored salvage resource; steel was an authored future processed output. No new metal/refinery chain is proven live by these sources.

T44–T52 themes map to Forest/Lakeshore, Desert/Canyons, Underwater, Sky, Volcanic, Swamp, Ruins, Underground and Alien Frontier. Dry habitat routes, fixed bridges/lifts, no people on conveyors and finite relay project identity constrain new vehicles.
